blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Covers critical developments in Space and Research Institutions.
Details key Nuclear Power Plants and national power capabilities.
Focuses on ecological conservation through Wildlife Sanctuaries and National Parks.
Addresses protection standards for Coastal and Marine Environment ecosystems.
Highlights advancements, policies, and targets in Renewable Energy.
Physical Research Laboratory (PRL): Ahmedabad — premier space sciences institute; founded by Vikram Sarabhai in 1947; under Dept. of Space.
Space Application Centre (SAC): Ahmedabad — ISRO's key centre for satellite communication, earth observation. Developed payloads for Chandrayaan missions.
Institute of Plasma Research (IPR): Gandhinagar — nuclear fusion research; India's tokamak (Aditya, SST-1).
Nirma University, DAIICT (Dhirubhai Ambani Institute of ICT): Major technical universities in Gandhinagar.
Kakrapar Atomic Power Station: Surat district; on banks of Tapi river; CANDU-type (PHWR) reactors. India's first nuclear plant to use light water for cooling (1993).

cells: Only habitat of Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) in the world outside Africa
India's first marine national park (1982); corals, dugong, turtles
Blackbuck (Indian antelope); also home to wolves and raptors
Indian Wild Ass (Khur) — Equus hemionus khur; IUCN Near Threatened
Tiger, leopard, gaur; part of Western Ghats ecosystem

items: Gulf of Kutch: Marine National Park and Marine Sanctuary — India's first; coral reefs and rich biodiversity.
Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay): Rich in marine life; Narmada and Mahi rivers meet the sea here; known for tidal bore phenomenon.
Mangroves: Found along Gujarat's coast, particularly in Kutch and south Gujarat. Kutch has the largest mangrove area in Gujarat.
Olive Ridley Turtles: Nesting sites at Simar beach (Kutch) and other coastal areas.
Frequent match-the-following questions mapping Space Research Institutions to their respective cities.
State-wise locations of operational Nuclear Power Plants are highly tested in prelims.
Key biosphere reserves, National Parks, and Renewable Energy target years are critical exam highlights.

blocks.content: Gujarat is a leader in renewable energy in India.

items: Solar Energy: Charanka Solar Park (Patan district) — one of Asia's largest solar parks. Gujarat was the first state to adopt a Solar Power Policy (2009).
Wind Energy: Kutch and Saurashtra have high wind energy potential. Gujarat is among India's top wind energy states.
RE-Invest: Gujarat participates actively in national renewable energy summits.
Hydrogen Project: Gujarat is being developed as a hub for Green Hydrogen production.
